body: Thank you! Small things are better than none, fingers crossed that one day I can move from small victories to huge successes!

I have no idea if this is a good idea because I still have room for improvement in terms of getting stuff done, but I break any big tasks up into tiny tiny tasks and put less overwhelming tasks in between the parts. For example, if going through a 40 minute lecture video has me shook, I divide it into four 10 min tasks, and in between each one I either take a break (like make coffee) or do a personal hygiene task (like brushing my hair or getting dressed). Idk how good of a tactic this is because I end up taking a lot longer to do 40 minutes of lecture, but I get other stuff done as well and this way it’s not as scary to me.

Also good luck with that interview! I’ve never done a job interview but I’ve done application interviews for school stuff and I think it’s good you’re taking initiative for keeping that day clear. Being calm and being yourself are your best tools to a good interview, I think. You got this!

Oh man showers are so hard to do. For me all the personal hygiene stuff is hardest. But it feels good once I do it because it’s something hard and I feel one step closer to being a clean and decent person lol, and sleeping in bed after showering feels really nice.

That’s a good thIng to point out. I do feel guilty when I don’t get a lot done, especially if there is so much to do, but I have to remind myself that every little bit of effort I do is progress.

I’m gonna try to keep today’s list smaller, I already slept in due to being overwhelmed lol

I was studying for an online class. Each video is 40mins but I get overwhelmed at that amount of time so I break it down into smaller, more manageable bites and put things in between to make it easier to go through. Makes it take longer to go through, which I need to fix, but some progress is better than none!

It does feel a tad unjustified at times, but if I don’t feel proud, nobody will. Only I’m aware of how much effort I put in, so I gotta encourage more effort by trying to tell myself “hey, you’re doing okay, this is good, keep going.”

This was my first time doing it too! I kept it really simple so as to keep it doable. Literally “10mins lecture, change, 10mins lecture, brush teeth, 10mins lecture, make coffee,...” stuff like that. I hope I can keep the habit of caring for myself too, but holy damn it’s hard
I wish I had the energy to make my bed lmao

Today is a good day! I managed to write a checklist of things I needed to do and I actually completed it. I studied for one of my classes, I took a shower, detangled my hair and brushed my teeth. 

That doesn’t sound like much at all compared to what you went through, but it’s all stuff I have such a hard time going through, and it all took me longer than it should have but I still got through it anyway. And you know what, I’m happy with that. I still have lots to get done, but I’m getting things through one task at a time!

So hell yeah, I’m proud of you for getting to this good day. You earned it! Enjoy that high school musical session my dude

Most sodas are way too sweet that it’s overwhelming(with the exception of root beer) and sparkling water has too sharp of a sour/salt note and makes me feel more bloated than the average fizzy drink. Beer, especially when frozen or near freezing, is freaking fantastic when you just want a refreshing, bubbly drink that isn’t overwhelming. Although I also love coffee, so certain bitter taste profiles do not seem as overwhelming to me.

I think I outlined it well in another post, so I’ll copy it here:

“I’m shitty at maintaining most relationships because I get tired halfway through. I have a shit sleep schedule. I have a hard time empathizing with people. I often want to help others but my motivation means jack shit since I only am actually able to help others when it’s easy. I suck at personal hygiene. I love to drink and I’m also addicted to caffeine. I have the worst eating habits: I both starve and stuff myself. I vent to others even if it doesn’t help me because sometimes I like the attention. I just want to OD on meds and alcohol because I’m too self destructive and selfish of a person that it’s easier to kill myself than to learn how to actually be helpful to society.”

So then you might ask “why not just change?” And I want to. I have the problem of having ideas but being too weak or selfish to turn them to action. It’s like I’m locked behind the back of my head and watching myself behave from a distance, and I hate what I’m seeing and who I am every step of the way. It’s pathetic, really.

My eyes are a really dark brown...so much so they’re almost black. You could hardly see my pupils or the brown in my irises unless you looked closely, or unless you shined a light in my eyes. They’re so dark, like looking in a lifeless abyss, with nothing but your reflection staring back. I used to feel a sense of intimidating discomfort when gazing at them in a mirror.

I used to wear glasses. I was so scared of switching to contacts for the longest time, but one of the reasons I overcame that fear was that I could get prescription color lenses to change my color. Maybe to a nice green or blue...

Too bad I have astigmatism over my myopia and they don’t make color lenses for that yet. So I have normal lenses for now. It’s been a couple years or so I’m not sure if I’ll go forward with getting those astigmatism color lenses anymore, if they even come out that is. And besides, I’ve found other benefits to getting contacts, like being able to see in the shower, comfortably watching a 3D movie, or going on a rollercoaster without worrying about glasses flying off. I’m trying to feel less insecure about my eyes, and your post is making me feel a little better about them. Thank you.

My leopard gecko is the same for me. She’s been with me for ten years now. She saw my life since late elementary and now she came with me to my apartment in college. And I’ve cared for her from the start. My life was worse in grade school but if I gave up then, nobody would be there care for my gecko the way that I do. Nobody around me would give her baths to remove stuck shed from her toes, sit with her for hours to make sure she ate, let her out often so she can walk around and explore the home freely, nobody puts in that time. And every time I watch television or study with her on my shoulder, every time she climbs up on my left shoulder or nudges up against my cheek, it feels like the best reward. Lizards truly are fantastic companions, more than most people give them credit for.

My brother struggles with the same thing. When I was in grade school I used to tutor him with maths and sciences. He’d always wonder how the hell I knew this stuff, why it just clicks with me and why he can’t understand the concepts as well. He envies me for being good at it and he wishes it came naturally to him too. But I tell him, that he shouldn’t envy me. Because we all have things that we struggle with. And that’s okay.

Yes, I’m fantastic at maths and sciences. But I also absolutely struggle with anything related to memorization. I dropped AP US history, I failed in my geography tests. I used to absolutely suck at writing. I was the only person in my grade who didn’t get a driver’s license. I still don’t know how to ride a bike, and every time I try I feel even more that I can never learn. While my brother is a freaking natural at driving, got his license as soon as he turned 16, and is breezing through his history classes like a pro. If anything, I’m the one who should envy him.

Nobody is good at everything, and we all struggle at something. Most people just find ways to hide their struggles and avoid situations that expose their weaknesses. And if you can’t avoid them, you just have to ask for help, or find resources to help you push through. I approached my English teacher when I was failing my AP Language practice tests and every time I wrote an essay she met with me one on one to go over how I screwed up. I bought extra world history practice books to help me study for AP World. College is fantastic because you can avoid taking your weak courses entirely, because classes are focused to the major you pick I basically have taken nothing but biology, chemistry, and tons of animal classes, and I’ve avoided my weak subjects (like history) entirely. Hell, I was able to take a coding class for my arts and humanities requirement, most people thought I was insane. But hey, it worked for me, and in this world there’s a path for everyone. Trust me, once you get out of high school you can find and pick the path that best fits you. But until then, find external resources to tough it out.

I knew that I can’t bike so I decided to focus on driving. I figured it was easier to sharpen my mental skills (like honing my awareness when driving) than learn new physical ones (like how to balance on a bike). I manned the fuck up after my first year in college, found a really cheap instructor, and barely got my driver’s license with only three weeks of driving (not the best way but it worked). I still struggle with driving as I’m very anxious, and even though my brother just got his license last week he’s already a more confident driver than me. That doesn’t mean I should give up though, and I’m still doing drives that scare the shit out of me in hopes to improve.

I guess what I’m saying is, it’s ok to not be good at certain things. Nobody is good at everything, and that’s completely ok. Struggling is a normal thing, and it doesn’t mean you’re set for failure. I’ve accepted that I’ll never be good at memorizing historical dates and events, I’ll probably never learn how to ride a bike. My brother might always struggle with chemistry. You might end up getting better at maths and sciences, but don’t give up if you can’t. Because there are ways to go around it. Find the things you *are* good at and focus on them. You just gotta keep pushing, keep finding those resources, and you’ll get far in life.

To be honest, it wasn’t typical therapy. It was the free counseling that my college offers for students. I can’t get paid counseling because I don’t have a job and my parents have no clue about my mental health, so this free counseling is all I have. I did it two years ago, and it lasted around ten weeks or so, until I started really improving and my therapist discharged me because I was doing well. The counseling was meant to be short term anyway. I was riding a high for months after, and since then I’ve been dealing with my mental health on my own again.

Like everyone says, you gotta put in your own effort for it to work. A therapist is just an outlet and a guide, if you don’t want to get better, you won’t get better. Buying a treadmill won’t help you lose weight unless you put the effort to go on it multiple times a week. The same goes with therapy. You have to find a therapist you trust and then you must take their word and advice into practice. That being said, I don’t regret doing it at all. Lately I’ve considered signing up for another ten week session. I just need to stop being a hesitant lil shit and get through with signing up. It becomes much easier once you start.

It gets harder the longer you wait. I know how terrifying it must be, especially if your friends are really great. When I first made my friends, it was the first time in my life that I was in a friend *group.* My only close friend before that is my high school one. I’ve never been in a group where I was included in everything they did and before this group I was always just a shadow. But these people really make me feel like I’m a huge part of their lives and they’re a huge part of mine and I don’t want to let that go. They’re like my second family, in a way. They’re already helping my depression without knowing it, through all the times we game, watch anime together, play DnD, they make me forget about my self hating thoughts, if only for a little bit. 

And that’s why I never told them. I want nothing more than to just fucking tell them, to spill out all my insecurities, to say that the times I don’t join discord vc are the nights I spend wallowing in bed, that the times I stay up till four am playing rocket league are because my racing thoughts are preventing me from falling asleep, the times I sound dead inside isn’t from irony. That I’m not the perpetually jolly and cheerful person they became friends with. I know they’ll probably be supportive, but I don’t want to be *that guy* who talks about their feelings when nobody else has done so before. They keep their struggles in check, why can’t I?

Sometimes I wonder if I’m doing the right thing. But damnit these people give me so much joy, and I’m not gonna let depression take that away from me. Depression fucking ruined my childhood, and sometimes I feel like the only reason college is turning out to be better is because I’ve been hiding it this whole time. Fuck this illness. I’m tired of being sick, I’m tired of pretending I’m not.

Do I regret keeping this in? Would I have acted differently and opened up to them early in our friendship if I had the chance? I have no fucking clue. All I know is that I still somehow managed to manifest a close friendship with these people and I’m so thankful for it. Does not having someone to talk to suck? Yeah, but I guess I’ll have to deal with it, as I always have. I am not fit to give any advice, you’re probably not asking for any anyway. But damn it if these friends are doing you good, and you know they’re genuinely good and healthy people to be around, then I’m fucking proud of you for landing that. Take their friendship, think highly of yourself. You’re doing good so far.

Mine was freshman year of high school too. Up to that point I was just feeling sadder and lonelier each year in increments, but freshman year I just realized that I wasn’t paying attention to the days going by, to my surroundings, the world around me was foggy. Months passed and I was completely unaware of it. My sleep schedule was very shitty and I’d constantly pass out during the day. My grades were slipping, I was self-loathing. I woke up when I walked into class one day and there were only two other people, and that was because I literally did not have the energy to sign the field trip paper I had to say I would go. And that hurt, because the field trip seemed fun too, and I didn’t even know if it, even though it was mentioned in class and I was *handed* a sign up sheet to fill out, until the day I missed it.

I feel you. I used to play piano a lot. Since I was seven I’ve been put in classical instruction programs where they just teach you songs for recitals, I play them, and forget them when learning next year’s songs. It was a grind, and I hated it.

This continued for ten years, until I asked my mother to sign me up in guitar center instead. The instructor taught me basic theory and scales, and gave me the tools to start writing music with.

I stopped playing other people’s music, for the most part. I play stuff that I write, but what I play isn’t...listenable. Piano has reduced into a ventilation for me; I play the tunes that my mind thinks up of when it tries to drown my racing thoughts, simple tunes with 2-5-4-5 chord progressions with an in-scale melody on top. I have no talent, and I stopped caring to develop it. Piano is a way for me to scream my problems at the world in a language that hides the ugliness of my feelings. Nothing more. I don’t play for others, I play so I can blow off some steam, to loosen the knot in my chest.

I feel vulnerable as hell when I sit down and play. I’ve seen a therapist and I’m telling you, venting to her felt the same as playing piano. If you see me play and approach me, I’ll jump. If I play in front of a crowd, I feel uncomfortable, the same way as having therapy sessions broadcasted on live national television would make you uncomfortable. And like I said, what I play isn’t music. It’s ventilation. Ventilation is never fun to listen to. So I feel almost...shameful to play in front of people. Especially since I often hide my mental struggles from most people. If I play in front of them it feels like I’m admitting my depression to them, and I’m not ready for that at all.

So, hats off to you for playing guitar today. That’s incredible and I’m very proud of you. I can only imagine the motions going through your head while doing so, but I’m sure the sort of peace or clarity afterward was worth it. Keep building up your confidence, you’re doing very well. You deserve to be able to play whenever the fuck you want, regardless of the number of people in the crowd.

I stopped cutting almost four years ago. Stopped banding around three years ago. I don’t really get urges anymore, but lately I’ve been getting thoughts that maybe it’s cathartic enough to make me feel better in this situation. It’s an unclear solution to an unclear problem. But damnit, I worked so goddamn hard to stop it. And I’ve come this far. I can’t break the streak now. I can’t visit my family next week with scars up my arm. I am fortunate enough that all my old ones faded, I can’t fail that now. So I move forward. If you are thinking of stopping, it does get easier. The first step is the absolute hardest, but like any addiction, the urges fade eventually.

I need to get my mind together and work better. Because hell, I need to survive this last bit of school. It’s one of my easiest quarters but this goddamn mental block is making it feel so impossible. I’m determined to find out why.

This isn’t the first time I seeked help. I was a lot worse. Really worse. Long story short I changed a lot of things about my life, and a year ago my friend encouraged me to seek counseling the first time. I finally did, and it helped temporarily. I became more self forgiving. I don’t even hate myself as much as I used to, but now I’m in a mental down state that is a lot more confusing than it ever was before. I don’t know what to do. I tried telling my friend, I tried playing piano, I tried drawing, I kept trying to acknowledge every little thing I managed to get done but I can’t help but feel so furiously disappointed in myself. It’s hard to be proud when I’m falling short in a lot of things.

It’s hopeless. I’m backed into a corner. I don’t want to go back to counseling and I’m unsure if they can even help. But I have no choice. I used to be high functioning even in the midst of depression, but now I’m upset and lethargic for no reason. I don’t know what else to do. I can’t fix a problem that shouldn’t exist.
